module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: $p$-adic Littlewood Conjecture

This is the $p$-adic analogue of the Littlewood conjecture, posed by de Mathan and
Teulié. A liminf-based formulation also appears in the file
`FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/LittlewoodConjecture.lean` as `padic_littlewood_conjecture`.

*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [dMT04] de Mathan, Bernard, and Olivier Teulié. "Problèmes diophantiens simultanés."
    Monatshefte für Mathematik 143.3 (2004): 229-245.
  - [EK07] Einsiedler, Manfred, and Dmitry Kleinbock. "Measure rigidity and $p$-adic
    Littlewood-type problems." Compositio Mathematica 143.3 (2007): 689-702.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Bugeaud08

/--
Problem 10.8 ($p$-adic Littlewood conjecture). For every real number $\xi$ and
every prime number $p$,
$$\inf_{q \ge 1} q \cdot \lVert q \xi \rVert \cdot |q|_p = 0,$$
where $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ denotes the distance to the nearest integer and
$|\cdot|_p$ denotes the $p$-adic absolute value. Posed by de Mathan and
Teulié [dMT04].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_8 (ξ : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    sInf {x : ℝ | ∃ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q ∧
      x = q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)} = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
The quadratic case of Problem 10.8. de Mathan and Teulié [dMT04] solved the
$p$-adic Littlewood conjecture for quadratic real numbers.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_8.variants.quadratic (ξ : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hξ : (minpoly ℚ ξ).natDegree = 2) :
    sInf {x : ℝ | ∃ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q ∧
      x = q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)} = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
The exceptional set for Problem 10.8 has Hausdorff dimension zero (Einsiedler
and Kleinbock [EK07].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_8.variants.exceptional_set_dimH_zero (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    dimH {ξ : ℝ | Filter.atTop.liminf
      (fun q : ℕ ↦ q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)) ≠ 0} = 0 := by
  sorry

end Bugeaud08

reformulations.difference: The exceptional set is written as {ξ | Filter.atTop.liminf (fun q : ℕ ↦ q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)) ≠ 0}. That is Mathlib's conditionally-complete-lattice liminf over q ∈ ℕ, which is EK07's form (e:MTm). The book's Theorem 2.26, and Problem 10.8 which the docstring names, define the exceptional set as the ξ that fail (2.34), i.e. inf_{q≥1} q‖qξ‖|q|_p = 0, which is the `sInf` form used in `problem_10_8`. Mathlib's `liminf` on ℝ can also return a junk value (0) when the sequence is not cobounded.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let u(q) = q|q|_p‖qξ‖. First, the Lean liminf is a genuine liminf. We have u ≥ 0, and u(p^k) = ‖p^k ξ‖ ≤ 1/2 for every k, so the sequence is bounded below and cobounded, and the liminf lies in [0, 1/2]; no junk value is reachable. Second, liminf = 0 ⇔ inf_{q≥1} u(q) = 0. (⇒) The infimum is at most the liminf and at least 0. (⇐) If ξ is rational, u vanishes on every multiple of its denominator. If ξ is irrational, u(q) > 0 for all q ≥ 1, so values below any ε > 0 must occur at arbitrarily large q. Proved in Lean without sorry: `liminf_eq_zero_iff_sInf_eq_zero` (for every ξ and prime p) and the set equality `exceptional_set_eq` between the file's set and {ξ | sInf {x | ∃ q ≥ 1, x = ...} ≠ 0}. So the variant states exactly the book's Theorem 2.26 (and, literally, EK07 Theorem 1.1).

sources_consulted: https://staff.dc.uba.ar/becher/aa/Bugeaud2012.pdf (Bugeaud, Distribution Modulo One and Diophantine Approximation, CUP 2012: Section 2.6 'A conjecture of de Mathan and Teulié' pp. 39-41, incl. (2.34), Theorems 2.24-2.27; Chapter 10 p. 215, Problem 10.8; bibliography entries [277] and [483])
https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0506514 (Einsiedler-Kleinbock, Measure rigidity and p-adic Littlewood-type problems: LaTeX source, introduction and Theorem 1.1)
https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12611 (Schleischitz, Disproof of the uniform Littlewood conjecture: abstract)
review.notes:
No misformalizations and no status issues found. Details by declaration:

`problem_10_8` matches Bugeaud's Problem 10.8 (p. 215) and (2.34) word for word: "For every real number ξ and every prime number p, we have inf_{q≥1} q·‖qξ‖·|q|_p = 0", with |p|_p = p^{-1}. That is `padicNorm`, and ‖·‖ is `distToNearestInt` = |x − round x|. The conclusion is `sInf … = 0`, so the junk value of `sInf` (empty or unbounded-below sets) would make it trivially true. I checked in Lean that this cannot happen: the set is nonempty (q = 1) and bounded below by 0. So `sInf` is the genuine infimum. The statement also holds trivially for rational ξ, as the book remarks; I checked that in Lean too. `research open` is still correct: papers from Aug 2026 (arXiv 2608.22078, 2609.26137) still treat the conjecture as open. arXiv 2603.12611 (2026) disproves only a *uniform* version of the p-adic Littlewood problem.

`variants.quadratic`: Bugeaud writes "(2.34) holds for every prime p and every quadratic number ξ, a result already proved in [483] (de Mathan–Teulié)". EK07 says the same ("de Mathan and Teulié showed that this property holds for elements of a quadratic number field"). The hypothesis `(minpoly ℚ ξ).natDegree = 2` means exactly "ξ is algebraic of degree 2". I checked in Lean that transcendental ξ are excluded (their `minpoly` is 0, with natDegree 0), that rational ξ are excluded (natDegree 1), and that ξ = √2 satisfies the hypothesis. `research solved` is correct. I could not open the dMT04 paper itself (Springer returns a JavaScript challenge), but two independent secondary sources confirm the quadratic result.

`variants.exceptional_set_dimH_zero`: this matches EK07 Theorem 1.1 literally ("The set of u ∈ ℝ which do not satisfy liminf_{q→∞} |q|·|q|_p·⟨qu⟩ = 0 has Hausdorff dimension zero", p fixed). It also matches Bugeaud's Theorem 2.26. The equivalence with the inf formulation is proved in Lean (see reformulations). `research solved` is correct.

Typo only (not a finding): the docstring of `exceptional_set_dimH_zero` is missing a closing parenthesis after "[EK07]".

Lean scratch files are in /workspace/review (sanity1.lean, equiv.lean, quad.lean). equiv.lean and quad.lean compile with no errors or warnings. sanity1.lean was an earlier draft whose last lemma fails to compile; the corrected versions of its lemmas are in equiv.lean. The checkout is unchanged: `lakefile.toml` and `run/` were already modified by the environment before I started.
